blocks.orig: Serengeti National Park is Africa’s most famous park due to the largest concentration of game on the continent and the migration of millions of wildebeest. The most impressive nature documentaries were shot in this beautiful park. ‘Serengeti’ comes from the Maasai language meaning ‘endless plains’ and nothing could describe it better. With almost 15,000 km2 (6,000 square miles), Serengeti National Park is the second-largest park in Tanzania.
blocks.html: No park in Africa is better known than Serengeti National Park, home to the continent’s largest concentration of game and the migration of millions of wildebeest. Many of the most memorable nature documentaries were filmed on these plains. The name ‘Serengeti’ is Maasai for ‘endless plains’, and no description fits better. Covering almost 15,000 km2 (6,000 square miles), Serengeti National Park ranks as the second-largest park in Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Witness the Great Wildebeest Migration in Serengeti National Park
blocks.html: Watch the Great Wildebeest Migration cross the Serengeti

blocks.orig: The annual wildebeest migration of more than a million wildebeest is probably Serengeti’s main attraction. It is a truly impressive sight to see all those mammals thunder across the Serengeti plains, crossing rivers, searching for water and fresh grass. Mega herds on the move stretch up to 40 kilometres long, covering a distance of some 1,000 kilometres. A dangerous journey for the wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles who need to outsmart their hungry predators. The biggest challenge is to cross the Mara and Grumeti Rivers, where giant crocodiles and fast flowing water awaits. The Great Migration is listed as one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World and clearly is the highlight for many visitors. As one of the world’s largest wildlife spectacles, this does not come as a surprise.
blocks.html: The yearly migration of over a million wildebeest is arguably the Serengeti’s biggest draw. Watching all those animals pound across the Serengeti plains, fording rivers in search of water and fresh grazing, is a genuinely impressive sight. The mega herds on the move can stretch up to 40 kilometres in length and travel some 1,000 kilometres in total. For the wildebeest, zebras and gazelles it is a perilous journey, as they must stay one step ahead of hungry predators. The toughest obstacle is crossing the Mara and Grumeti Rivers, where fast-flowing water and giant crocodiles lie in wait. Listed as one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World, the Great Migration is clearly the highlight for many visitors. Given that it ranks among the largest wildlife spectacles on earth, that is hardly surprising.

blocks.orig: You can witness the wildebeest migration anytime of the year, since the animals migrate in a circle between the Serengeti and Masai Mara (Kenya). The exact timing of the migration depends upon the rainfall patterns each year. Thanks to our experienced Your Tanzania Trip guides, we can make a fairly accurate prediction.
blocks.html: Because the animals move in a circle between the Serengeti and the Masai Mara (Kenya), the wildebeest migration can be seen at any time of year. When exactly the herds are where depends on each year’s rainfall. With the experience of our Your Tanzania Trip guides, we can predict it fairly accurately.

blocks.orig: Serengeti National Park offers so much more beauty than just the wildebeest migration. You can see a variety of landscapes and wildlife unlike anywhere else in Africa. The endless plains are home to more than 4,000 lions, 1,000 leopards, 225 cheetahs and 3,500 hyenas. It’s no surprise there are so many predators due to the abundance of wildebeest, zebras, gazelles, and buffalo. The Serengeti is also one of the best places to see the Big Five – rhino, buffalo, elephant, lion, and leopard. Almost all the famous African animals are present in this majestic park. This includes rare animal species like the pangolin, East African Oryx, rhino and African wild dog.
blocks.html: There is far more to Serengeti National Park than the wildebeest migration alone. Its mix of landscapes and wildlife is unlike anything else in Africa. More than 4,000 lions, 1,000 leopards, 225 cheetahs and 3,500 hyenas live on these endless plains. With such plentiful wildebeest, zebras, gazelles and buffalo around, that number of predators makes perfect sense. The Serengeti also ranks among the best places to see the Big Five – rhino, buffalo, elephant, lion and leopard. Nearly every well-known African animal can be found in this majestic park, including rare species such as the pangolin, East African Oryx, rhino and African wild dog.

blocks.orig: The captivating landscapes of Serengeti National Park vary from savannas with acacia trees and vast grasslands to rising mountains, lakes, and swamps. Each area is unique and has its own atmosphere. Because of its natural beauty and variety of plants and animals, the park is listed as UNESCO World Heritage Site. This place definitely touches your soul.
blocks.html: The scenery of Serengeti National Park is captivating and varied: acacia-dotted savannas and vast grasslands give way to rising mountains, lakes and swamps. Every area feels different and has an atmosphere of its own. Thanks to its natural beauty and the variety of its plant and animal life, the park holds UNESCO World Heritage status. It is a place that truly stays with you.

blocks.orig: My name is Samson, and I have been a guide at Serengeti National Park for 18 years. Most of our guests are impressed to see so many lions, but also leopards and cheetahs. Of course, the Great Wildebeest Migration is an outstanding spectacle to witness for all our guests. The wildlife in Serengeti National Park is unmatched anywhere else.
blocks.html: I am Samson, and for 18 years I have worked as a guide in Serengeti National Park. What impresses most of our guests is the sheer number of lions, along with the leopards and cheetahs. And naturally, the Great Wildebeest Migration is an exceptional spectacle for everyone who visits. Nowhere else can match the wildlife of Serengeti National Park.
